## Natural history notes

A small grass-veneer moth characterized by narrow tan to straw-colored wings marked with bold pale longitudinal stripes and darker brown lines that give it a clean, striped appearance. In Florida, it is found in grassy habitats such as prairies, pine flatwoods, roadsides, lawns, marsh edges, fields, and other open areas where grasses are common. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on grasses or related low plants, often living close to the ground in silk shelters or folded blades.
